raw_response:
I will keep this year simple and steady. In Quzhou County, the land, water, and weather fit winter wheat followed by summer maize better than anything else for me. I am 66, so I do not want to spread myself across too many crops or chase a risky cash crop. I want the cropping pattern I know well, that matches local machines, local input shops, and the rainfall pattern here: wheat uses more irrigation in the dry season, and maize catches the summer rain. I will put all my land into the wheat-maize rotation on the same fields. For seed, I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I care more about stable yield and easier management than saving seed myself. For fertilizer, I will not push it too hard. I will use moderate nitrogen, with phosphorus and potassium kept in balance, because too much nitrogen costs money and can make the crop soft or wasteful. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage before wheat because it is familiar and practical, and I will use no-tillage for summer maize after wheat harvest to save time and hold moisture. For irrigation, I will water wheat about three times if the season is normal, mainly around key growth stages, while maize usually only needs one irrigation or a rescue watering because summer rain does most of the work. I will keep pesticide use limited but timely, mainly one to two herbicide or disease-insect control passes in each crop, because I want clean fields without spending too much. My goal is not the highest possible yield. My goal is a stable crop, lower labor pressure, and a safe harvest.
